departments.name: Business Administration Department
departments.description: Manages academic programs in business, finance, entrepreneurship, and commerce. Policies govern curriculum design, academic integrity, faculty conduct, and industry engagement.

departments.name: Information Technology Department
departments.description: Manages IT infrastructure, digital systems, data governance, and cybersecurity for the entire institution, aligned with Nepal's National Cyber Security Policy 2023 and Electronic Transactions Act 2063.

departments.name: Management Department
departments.description: Oversees programs in organizational management, leadership, and strategy. Policies govern faculty development, curriculum delivery, research output, and community engagement.

departments.name: Social Sciences Department
departments.description: Covers sociology, psychology, political science, and economics. Policies emphasize research ethics, human subjects protection, DEI, and data management.

departments.name: Hospitality Department
departments.description: Offers programs in hotel management, food and beverage management, and tourism. Policies govern industry placements, training lab operations, food safety, and tourism curriculum.

departments.name: Finance Department
departments.description: Governs all institutional financial processes including budgeting, procurement, tuition management, audit, and reporting.

departments.name: Human Resource Department
departments.description: Manages the full employment lifecycle for all faculty and staff in compliance with Nepal's Labour Act 2074 and Labour Rules 2075.

departments.name: Quality Assurance and Accreditation Office
departments.description: Coordinates institutional quality assurance, accreditation compliance, self-study processes, and continuous improvement aligned with UGC Nepal's QAA framework.

policies.title: Academic Program Review and Approval Policy
policies.description: Defines the process for initiating, reviewing, modifying, or discontinuing academic programs. Programs must undergo internal review every five years and must align with national higher education standards and affiliating university regulations.
policies.scope: All undergraduate and postgraduate programs offered by the department.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Initiates review cycle, forms review committee.
Evaluates curriculum relevance, learning outcomes, and resource requirements.
Approves or rejects proposed changes.
Updates program catalog upon approval.

policies.decisionContext: Used when: proposing a new program, revising an existing curriculum, responding to accreditation feedback, or phasing out an underperforming program.
legalBasis: University Grants Commission (UGC) Program Approval Guidelines
constraints: Changes require Academic Council approval at least one semester before implementation.
All revisions must be reflected in the updated course catalog submitted to the affiliating university.

outcomes.label: Approved
outcomes.action: Program is updated in catalog and communicated to students.

outcomes.label: Rejected
outcomes.action: Review committee receives written feedback and must revise proposal.

outcomes.label: Deferred
outcomes.action: Additional stakeholder consultation required.

policies.title: Academic Integrity and Anti-Plagiarism Policy
policies.description: Establishes standards for academic honesty, defines forms of academic misconduct (plagiarism, cheating, fabrication, collusion), and outlines investigation and disciplinary procedures.
policies.scope: All enrolled students across all programs.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Detect and report academic misconduct.
Investigate reported cases.
Issue final decision on minor violations.
Handle appeals and severe violations.

policies.decisionContext: Triggered when faculty suspect or detect academic misconduct in assignments, examinations, or research submissions.
constraints: Plagiarism detection tool must be used for all major assessments.
Investigations must be completed within 21 working days of initial report.

outcomes.label: Minor violation (first offence)
outcomes.action: Grade penalty (zero on the assignment).

outcomes.label: Moderate violation
outcomes.action: Repeat of the course.

outcomes.label: Severe or repeat violation
outcomes.action: Suspension or expulsion. All decisions are recorded in the student's academic file.

policies.title: Industry Partnership and MOU Governance Policy
policies.description: Governs the initiation, approval, management, and renewal of Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with industry partners, NGOs, and professional bodies for internships, guest lectures, joint research, and project collaboration.
policies.scope: All formal institutional partnerships involving the Business Administration Department.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Proposes and recommends MOUs.
Reviews financial terms.
Validates legal compliance.
Signs and approves MOUs.
Tracks personnel obligations arising from MOUs.

policies.decisionContext: Required when formalizing any collaboration for internship placement, sponsored research, or co-curricular activities with an external entity.
constraints: MOUs must be reviewed and renewed every three years.
All MOUs must be reviewed by the legal/compliance officer before signing.

outcomes.label: Signed MOU
outcomes.action: Activates collaboration plan and assigns a departmental liaison.

outcomes.label: Expired without renewal
outcomes.action: Partnership activities suspended until renewal is processed.

policies.title: Student Internship and Practicum Policy
policies.description: Defines the requirements, placement procedures, supervision responsibilities, and assessment criteria for mandatory internships and practicums that are part of the Business Administration curriculum.
policies.scope: All students enrolled in programs with a mandatory internship component.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Identifies and approves placement organizations, manages placement records.
Conducts mid-term visits and assesses performance.
Submit weekly logs and a final internship report.
Maintains internship MOU records.

policies.decisionContext: Applied when placing students for internship, evaluating internship performance, or resolving disputes between students and host organizations.
constraints: Internship duration must meet minimum credit-hour requirements.
Host organizations must be pre-approved.
Students failing the internship component must repeat the placement.

outcomes.label: Pass
outcomes.action: Internship credits are awarded and recorded in the transcript.

outcomes.label: Fail
outcomes.action: Student must re-enrol in the internship component in the following semester.

policies.title: Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resources Policy
policies.description: Defines permitted and prohibited uses of all institutional IT resources including computers, networks, internet access, email systems, and licensed software. All users must comply as a condition of access.
policies.scope: All students, faculty, administrative staff, and third-party contractors using institutional IT resources.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Maintains and enforces the AUP.
Monitors network usage for violations.
Must read, sign, and comply with the AUP on joining.
Incorporates AUP compliance into onboarding and service contracts.

policies.decisionContext: Applied during onboarding, when investigating potential misuse, or when reviewing access privileges.
constraints: Non-compliance may result in suspension of IT access.
The AUP must be reviewed and re-signed by all users annually.
Personal use of institutional resources is permitted within defined limits.

outcomes.label: Violation confirmed
outcomes.action: Access suspended pending investigation; disciplinary proceedings initiated.

outcomes.label: Policy breach not confirmed
outcomes.action: Access restored with written advisory.

policies.title: Data Classification and Information Security Policy
policies.description: Establishes a data classification framework (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and defines handling, storage, access control, and retention requirements for each classification level. Aligns with Nepal's Data Act 2079.
policies.scope: All institutional data generated, processed, or stored by the college in any format.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Oversees classification compliance and annual audits.
Implement technical controls for each data class.
Ensure departmental data is properly classified and handled.
Follow data handling procedures for their classification level.

policies.decisionContext: Used when onboarding new data systems, responding to a data request, conducting an audit, or investigating a suspected data breach.
constraints: Restricted data cannot be transmitted via unencrypted channels.
Retention periods: Student records — 10 years post-graduation; Financial records — 7 years; HR records — 5 years post-separation.

outcomes.label: Non-compliance identified
outcomes.action: Immediate remediation required; reported to DPO.

outcomes.label: Data breach confirmed
outcomes.action: Incident response plan activated; affected parties notified within 72 hours.

policies.title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Policy
policies.description: Provides a structured procedure for detecting, reporting, containing, investigating, and recovering from cybersecurity incidents including ransomware, phishing, DDoS attacks, and data breaches.
policies.scope: All institutional IT systems, networks, and digital assets.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Leads containment and investigation.
Escalates critical incidents to college management.
Assesses data exposure and manages notification obligations.
Approves public communications regarding incidents.

policies.decisionContext: Activated upon confirmed or suspected cybersecurity incident. Severity levels (1–3) determine response timelines.
legalBasis: Nepal Police Cyber Bureau Reporting Guidelines
constraints: Level 1 incidents (critical) must be contained within 4 hours.
Reportable incidents must be escalated to the Nepal Cyber Bureau as required by national law.

outcomes.label: Incident resolved
outcomes.action: Post-incident report produced within 7 days; root cause documented; preventive measures implemented.

outcomes.label: Unresolved
outcomes.action: Escalated to national authorities and external forensic support engaged.

policies.title: Software Procurement and License Management Policy
policies.description: Governs the acquisition, registration, deployment, and audit of all software licenses used by the institution. Prevents unauthorized software use and ensures compliance with vendor agreements.
policies.scope: All software installed or used on institutional hardware or institutional cloud platforms.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Manages license procurement and renewal calendar.
Submit software needs requests with justification.
Approves budget allocation for software licenses.
Maintains software asset register.

policies.decisionContext: Required when purchasing new software, renewing existing licenses, auditing installed software, or investigating unlicensed software use.
constraints: No software may be installed on institutional devices without IT Department approval.
Open-source software must be vetted for license compatibility before use.
Annual license audit must be conducted.

outcomes.label: Unauthorized software found
outcomes.action: Immediate removal and departmental warning.

outcomes.label: Non-compliant license
outcomes.action: Cease use until properly licensed or replaced with approved alternative.

policies.title: IT Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Policy
policies.description: Defines recovery time objectives (RTO), recovery point objectives (RPO), backup procedures, and continuity plans to ensure institutional systems remain operational or are quickly restored after disruption.
policies.scope: All critical IT systems including student information system (SIS), financial management system, email, and learning management system (LMS).

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Owns the Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP).
Executes and verifies daily backups.
Declares business continuity events.
Identify and report critical process dependencies.

policies.decisionContext: Activated when a major system failure, natural disaster, or cyberattack causes significant disruption to institutional operations.
legalBasis: Nepal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act 2074
constraints: Critical systems RTO: 4 hours; RPO: 24 hours.
Backups must be stored off-site or in a geographically separate cloud region.
DR drills must be conducted annually.

outcomes.label: Successful recovery
outcomes.action: Systems restored within RTO; incident report produced.

outcomes.label: Failed recovery
outcomes.action: Escalation to senior management and activation of manual continuity procedures.

policies.title: Faculty Development and Continuing Professional Education Policy
policies.description: Defines the institution's commitment to ongoing faculty skill enhancement through training, workshops, conference participation, sabbaticals, and higher study sponsorship. Establishes entitlements, application procedures, and return-of-service obligations.
policies.scope: All permanent and contract faculty members of the department.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Approves CPD plans and nominates faculty for programs.
Manages leave, travel advance, and return-of-service records.
Allocates CPD budget.
Submits CPD plan, attends programs, and submits post-training report.

policies.decisionContext: Used when approving faculty training requests, awarding conference travel grants, or managing sabbatical applications.
constraints: Faculty sponsored for degree-level study must serve a return-of-service period equal to the duration of sponsorship.
CPD budget shall not exceed 5% of the departmental annual budget.
Faculty must submit a utilization report within 30 days of returning.

outcomes.label: Approved
outcomes.action: Leave and funding granted; return-of-service bond signed.

outcomes.label: Rejected
outcomes.action: Written justification provided; alternative development options suggested.

policies.title: Strategic Departmental Planning Policy
policies.description: Establishes the annual and medium-term (3–5 year) planning process for the department, including setting objectives, aligning with institutional strategy, monitoring KPIs, and reporting to senior management.
policies.scope: Management Department administration, faculty, and support staff.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Leads planning process and approves final plan.
Contribute to program-level goals.
Ensures plan aligns with accreditation criteria.
Reviews and endorses the department's strategic plan.

policies.decisionContext: Used during annual planning cycles, in response to QA audit findings, or when the institution revises its strategic framework.
constraints: Plans must be submitted to the College Principal by the end of the first month of each academic year.
KPIs must be measurable and linked to resource allocations in the departmental budget request.

outcomes.label: Plan approved
outcomes.action: Resources allocated accordingly.

outcomes.label: Plan returned
outcomes.action: Department must revise within 14 days.

outcomes.label: Unsubmitted
outcomes.action: Subject to administrative review.

policies.title: Graduate Research and Thesis Supervision Policy
policies.description: Defines the requirements for thesis/dissertation registration, supervisor assignment, ethical review, progress monitoring, examination, and degree conferment for postgraduate management programs.
policies.scope: All students enrolled in Master's or M.Phil. programs requiring a thesis or dissertation.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Assigns supervisors; maintains progress records.
Guides research design, reviews drafts, approves for submission.
Reviews research proposals involving human subjects.
Coordinates external examiners and defense scheduling.

policies.decisionContext: Applied at thesis registration, ethical review, mid-point progress review, and final submission/defense stages.
legalBasis: Nepal National Research and Innovation Policy
constraints: Students must submit a research proposal for ethics review within 60 days of thesis registration.
Supervisors may not supervise more than 6 active thesis students simultaneously.
Thesis must be submitted in the format prescribed by the affiliating university.

outcomes.label: Ethical clearance granted
outcomes.action: Student proceeds with data collection.

outcomes.label: Minor thesis revisions
outcomes.action: Resubmit within 30 days.

outcomes.label: Major revisions
outcomes.action: 6-month extension granted.

outcomes.label: Rejection
outcomes.action: Student must re-register topic.

policies.title: Human Subjects Research and Institutional Review Policy
policies.description: Establishes the framework for ethical review and approval of all research involving human participants. Based on principles of informed consent, voluntary participation, confidentiality, and minimization of harm.
policies.scope: All faculty-led, student-led, or externally commissioned research involving human participants conducted under the department's affiliation.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Reviews proposals, grants clearance, monitors active studies.
Submits proposal, obtains informed consent, reports adverse events.
Ensures all research in the department complies with this policy.
Voluntary, informed consent must be documented.

policies.decisionContext: Triggered at research proposal stage; re-triggered for major protocol amendments or adverse event reports.
legalBasis: Nepal Health Research Council Act (for health-related social research)
constraints: No data collection may begin without written REC clearance.
Research involving minors (under 18) or vulnerable groups requires enhanced review.
Informed consent forms must be available in Nepali and English.

outcomes.label: Clearance granted
outcomes.action: Research proceeds; REC registers study and monitors timeline.

outcomes.label: Conditional clearance
outcomes.action: Researcher must address listed conditions before proceeding.

outcomes.label: Rejected
outcomes.action: Researcher receives written reasons; may revise and resubmit.

policies.title: Research Data Management and Archiving Policy
policies.description: Defines requirements for the collection, storage, protection, sharing, and archiving of research data across the project lifecycle to ensure data integrity, reproducibility, and compliance.
policies.scope: All research data produced by faculty and students affiliated with the Social Sciences Department.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Produces a Data Management Plan (DMP) before data collection.
Provides secure storage infrastructure.
Approves DMP; ensures data archiving after project completion.
Verifies data handling complies with consent agreements.

policies.decisionContext: Applied at research proposal stage (DMP creation), during active research (data security), and post-project (archiving and disposal).
constraints: Raw data must be retained for a minimum of 5 years post-publication.
Personally identifiable information (PII) must be anonymized before archiving.
Data from studies involving human subjects cannot be shared publicly without re-consent or full anonymization.

outcomes.label: Non-compliant data handling identified
outcomes.action: Immediate remediation required; REC notified.

outcomes.label: Data loss or breach
outcomes.action: Incident response procedure activated; participants notified as required.

policies.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) in Curriculum and Hiring Policy
policies.description: Embeds DEI principles into course design, teaching practices, and faculty hiring to reflect Nepal's socially and culturally diverse student population, including representation of Janajati, Dalit, Madhesi, women, and persons with disabilities.
policies.scope: All academic programs, teaching activities, and faculty recruitment processes within the department.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Ensures DEI principles are reflected in course syllabi and faculty hiring.
Design courses that represent diverse perspectives and use inclusive teaching methods.
Incorporates DEI criteria in job descriptions and selection panels.

policies.decisionContext: Applied during syllabus review, accreditation self-study, and faculty hiring rounds.
legalBasis: Constitution of Nepal 2072 — Right to Equality (Art. 18), Right against Untouchability (Art. 24)
constraints: At least 33% representation of women in departmental hiring panels as required by law.
All new course syllabi must include at least two assigned texts by Nepali or South Asian authors.

outcomes.label: DEI audit pass
outcomes.action: No action required.

outcomes.label: Gap identified
outcomes.action: Action plan with timeline required; reported to QA Office.

outcomes.label: Discrimination complaint
outcomes.action: Investigated under the college's Grievance and Harassment Policy.

policies.title: Hotel Management Internship and Placement Policy
policies.description: Defines the structure, duration, placement criteria, supervision framework, and assessment methods for mandatory hotel and food service internships that form a core component of all hospitality programs.
policies.scope: All students enrolled in Bachelor's or Diploma programs in Hotel Management or Tourism.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Identifies and approves hospitality industry partners; manages placement logistics.
Conducts minimum two on-site visits; evaluates student performance.
Submit bi-weekly logs and a final reflective report.
Maintains placement MOU records.

policies.decisionContext: Applied when placing students, evaluating performance mid-placement, resolving workplace disputes, or approving alternative placement due to unavailability.
constraints: Internship must be a minimum of 16 weeks for Bachelor's programs.
Host organizations must be registered with the relevant authority (e.g., Department of Tourism).
Students must pass a food safety orientation before placement in food-service roles.

outcomes.label: Pass
outcomes.action: Internship credits awarded; host organization feedback recorded.

outcomes.label: Fail
outcomes.action: Student must repeat the placement.

outcomes.label: Exceptional performance
outcomes.action: Letter of commendation issued; eligible for departmental award.

policies.title: Training Kitchen and Hospitality Lab Usage Policy
policies.description: Regulates safe access, hygiene standards, equipment use, and supervision requirements for the department's training kitchen and hospitality simulation facilities.
policies.scope: All students, faculty, and visiting instructors using the training kitchen, mock front-desk, and event simulation labs.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Oversees day-to-day operations; ensures compliance with food safety standards.
Provide induction training before first lab session.
Follow hygiene protocols and equipment handling guidelines.
Maintains point-of-sale and property management system (PMS) simulation software.

policies.decisionContext: Applied during lab scheduling, after a safety incident, or in response to hygiene inspection findings.
legalBasis: Food Safety and Quality Authority of Nepal (DFTQC) Standards
Nepal Standard for Hotels and Restaurants
constraints: No student may use kitchen equipment without completing the mandatory safety induction.
All perishable ingredients must be stored according to temperature control standards.
Lab capacity is limited to defined maximum occupancy per session.

outcomes.label: Safety violation
outcomes.action: Session suspended; remedial training required; incident logged.

outcomes.label: Hygiene inspection failed
outcomes.action: Lab closed until deficiencies are corrected and re-inspection passed.

outcomes.label: Equipment damage
outcomes.action: Assessment of liability; replacement or repair costs assigned per policy.

policies.title: Sustainable Tourism and Responsible Hospitality Curriculum Policy
policies.description: Requires all hospitality programs to integrate sustainability, responsible tourism, and cultural sensitivity principles into course content, assessments, and field activities, consistent with Nepal's role as a major tourism destination.
policies.scope: All programs and modules offered by the Hospitality Department.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Ensures sustainability content is embedded in all program specifications.
Design learning activities that develop students' understanding of environmental impact, cultural heritage, and community-based tourism.
Verifies sustainability integration during curriculum review.

policies.decisionContext: Applied during curriculum review cycles, program accreditation self-studies, and when developing new elective modules.
constraints: At least 20% of program-level learning outcomes must explicitly address sustainability or responsible tourism.
Guest lecturer input from community tourism practitioners must be included at least once per academic year per program.

outcomes.label: Full integration confirmed
outcomes.action: Program meets QA sustainability criterion.

outcomes.label: Partial integration
outcomes.action: Action plan required with timeline for full compliance.

outcomes.label: Non-integration
outcomes.action: Program placed on curriculum improvement watch list; QA oversight increased.

policies.title: Annual Budget Formulation and Approval Policy
policies.description: Defines the annual budget planning cycle, departmental request procedures, resource allocation criteria, and approval workflow for the institution's operating and capital expenditure budget.
policies.scope: All departments and cost centres within the institution.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Circulates budget call circular; consolidates departmental submissions.
Submit budget proposals with justification and activity plans by the deadline.
Reviews proposals against institutional priorities; recommends final budget.
Approves the budget and presents it to the Governing Board.

policies.decisionContext: Conducted annually before the start of the fiscal year (Shrawan 1 in Nepal). Supplementary budget requests may be made mid-year in exceptional circumstances.
legalBasis: Financial Procedures and Fiscal Accountability Act 2076 (FPFAA)
constraints: Budget requests must be submitted by Chaitra 15 each year.
Unfunded requests are automatically deferred to the next cycle.
Departmental budget cannot be increased mid-year without Finance Committee approval.

outcomes.label: Budget approved
outcomes.action: Funds released to departments in quarterly tranches.

outcomes.label: Over-budget proposal
outcomes.action: Department must revise and resubmit with reduced scope.

outcomes.label: Supplementary request approved
outcomes.action: Subject to available institutional reserves.

policies.title: Procurement and Expenditure Control Policy
policies.description: Establishes procurement thresholds, competitive bidding requirements, vendor approval processes, and expenditure authorization levels to ensure transparent and accountable use of institutional funds.
policies.scope: All procurement of goods, services, and works undertaken by the institution.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Manages tender processes; maintains vendor register.
Verifies budget availability before procurement is authorized.
Submit justified purchase requests.
Reviews high-value procurements.
Approves procurements above defined threshold.

policies.decisionContext: Applied for all institutional purchases. Thresholds determine whether direct purchase, quotation-based purchase, or public tender is required.
legalBasis: Financial Procedures and Fiscal Accountability Act 2076
constraints: Purchases above NPR 500,000 require a minimum of three competitive quotations.
Purchases above NPR 5,000,000 require public tender.
No splitting of procurements to avoid tender thresholds is permitted.

outcomes.label: Procurement approved
outcomes.action: Purchase order issued to vendor; contract signed for works/services.

outcomes.label: Irregularity identified
outcomes.action: Procurement suspended; internal audit notified.

outcomes.label: Vendor blacklisted
outcomes.action: Removed from approved register; reported to relevant authority.

policies.title: Tuition Fee, Scholarship, and Refund Policy
policies.description: Sets fee structures for all academic programs, defines scholarship eligibility and disbursement procedures, and establishes the tuition refund schedule for withdrawals and programme cancellations.
policies.scope: All enrolled and prospective students.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Maintains fee schedule; processes payments, scholarships, and refunds.
Reviews applications and awards scholarships based on criteria.
Confirms enrollment status for fee and refund calculations.
Nominate students for merit-based scholarships.

policies.decisionContext: Applied at semester commencement, upon student withdrawal, when issuing scholarship awards, and when auditing fee collection.
legalBasis: College Fee Schedule (approved by Governing Board)
constraints: Full refund: Withdrawal within 7 days of fee payment.
50% refund: Withdrawal between 8–30 days.
No refund: Withdrawal after 30 days.
Scholarship recipients who fail to maintain required GPA may have scholarship suspended pending review.

outcomes.label: Refund approved
outcomes.action: Processed within 15 working days.

outcomes.label: Refund denied
outcomes.action: Written reason provided; student may appeal to Finance Committee.

outcomes.label: Scholarship suspended
outcomes.action: Student notified in writing; eligible to appeal within 14 days.

policies.title: Internal Audit and Financial Control Policy
policies.description: Establishes the mandate, scope, methodology, and reporting requirements for the institution's internal audit function to ensure financial controls are operating effectively and institutional funds are used appropriately.
policies.scope: All financial transactions, assets, and processes of the institution.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Conducts risk-based audits; reports findings to management.
Implements audit recommendations.
Receives and acts on audit reports.
Reviews internal audit reports annually.

relatedEntities: External Auditor (Office of the Auditor General or licensed CA firm)
policies.decisionContext: Annual audit plan approved at the start of each fiscal year. Special audits triggered by complaints, anomalies, or Governing Board direction.
legalBasis: Financial Procedures and Fiscal Accountability Act 2076
Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN) Standards
constraints: Internal auditor must be independent of the Finance Officer.
Audit findings must be communicated to management within 30 days of field work completion.
Management must respond to audit findings within 21 days.

outcomes.label: Finding actioned
outcomes.action: Management letter closed; control improvement documented.

outcomes.label: Finding not actioned within deadline
outcomes.action: Escalated to College Principal and noted in next Governing Board report.

outcomes.label: Material misstatement found
outcomes.action: Referred to external authority if required.

policies.title: Recruitment, Selection, and Appointment Policy
policies.description: Defines the end-to-end procedure for advertising vacancies, screening applications, conducting interviews, making offers, and onboarding new employees for both academic and non-academic positions.
policies.scope: All permanent, contract, and part-time positions across the institution.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Advertises vacancies, manages application pool, coordinates selection process, issues offer letters.
Reviews applications, conducts interviews, recommends candidates.
Provides technical assessment criteria; participates in selection.
Approves appointments for senior positions.

relatedEntities: UGC (for faculty appointments at applicable ranks)
policies.decisionContext: Applied when a vacancy arises due to new position creation, resignation, retirement, or contract expiry.
legalBasis: Constitution of Nepal 2072 — Right against Discrimination
constraints: Selection committees must include at least one woman as required by constitutional reservation provisions.
All job advertisements must be published in at least one national newspaper and the institution's website.
Appointment letters must specify grade, salary, probation period, and terms of service.

outcomes.label: Candidate selected
outcomes.action: Offer letter issued; background verification completed; onboarding initiated.

outcomes.label: No suitable candidate
outcomes.action: Position re-advertised or temporarily filled by internal acting arrangement.

outcomes.label: Candidate rejects offer
outcomes.action: Next-ranked candidate considered or process restarted.

policies.title: Employee Performance Appraisal Policy
policies.description: Establishes the framework for annual performance appraisal of all staff, linking performance outcomes to salary increments, promotion recommendations, professional development opportunities, and corrective action plans.
policies.scope: All permanent and long-term contract employees.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Conducts mid-year and annual review; completes appraisal form.
Completes self-evaluation; participates in review discussion.
Manages appraisal calendar; processes outcomes.
Reviews aggregate performance data and approves promotion/increment recommendations.

policies.decisionContext: Conducted annually, with a mid-year check-in. Triggered additionally when an employee's performance falls below acceptable standards.
legalBasis: Labour Act 2074 — Section on performance and promotion
constraints: Appraisals must be completed within 60 days of the end of the academic year.
Staff rated 'Unsatisfactory' must be placed on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) within 30 days.
Salary increments are processed only after appraisal completion.

outcomes.label: Outstanding/Excellent
outcomes.action: Fast-track promotion consideration; CPD award eligible.

outcomes.label: Satisfactory
outcomes.action: Standard increment processed.

outcomes.label: Unsatisfactory
outcomes.action: PIP initiated; reviewed after 90 days.

outcomes.label: Persistent underperformance
outcomes.action: Disciplinary proceedings or contract non-renewal.

policies.title: Leave and Attendance Management Policy
policies.description: Defines all categories of leave entitlement (annual, sick, maternity, paternity, bereavement, study, special), attendance recording procedures, and the consequences of unauthorized absence.
policies.scope: All permanent and contract employees.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Maintains leave records; processes applications; tracks balances.
Approves routine leave requests within defined delegations.
Approves extended or exceptional leave requests.
Processes leave encashment where applicable.

policies.decisionContext: Applied when an employee applies for leave, when investigating unauthorized absence, or when auditing leave balances.
legalBasis: Labour Act 2074 — Chapter on leave entitlements
constraints: Annual leave: 18 days per year (accrual).
Sick leave: 12 days per year (non-encashable).
Maternity leave: 98 days (per Labour Act 2074).
Paternity leave: 15 days.
Leave exceeding entitlement is treated as leave without pay unless exceptional circumstances apply.

outcomes.label: Leave approved
outcomes.action: Record updated; substitute arrangement made if required.

outcomes.label: Leave denied
outcomes.action: Employee notified in writing with reason.

outcomes.label: Unauthorized absence
outcomes.action: Treated as leave without pay; repeated absence triggers disciplinary review.

policies.title: Workplace Grievance and Anti-Harassment Policy
policies.description: Establishes a safe, confidential mechanism for employees and students to raise complaints related to workplace harassment, discrimination, bullying, and unfair treatment, with defined investigation and resolution procedures.
policies.scope: All employees, students, and third parties in the institutional environment.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Receives complaints; initiates formal or informal resolution.
Conducts impartial investigation of formal complaints.
Reviews committee findings and issues final decision.
Maintains records and ensures resolution timelines are met.

policies.decisionContext: Activated upon receipt of a written or verbal complaint by any member of the institutional community.
legalBasis: Labour Act 2074 — grievance and disciplinary provisions
Gender Equality and State Restructuring Act (Nepal)
Constitution of Nepal 2072 — Right against Exploitation
constraints: Acknowledgment of complaint within 3 working days.
Informal resolution: within 21 days.
Formal investigation: within 45 days.
Confidentiality must be maintained throughout.
Retaliation against complainants is strictly prohibited and is itself a disciplinary offence.

outcomes.label: Complaint upheld
outcomes.action: Appropriate disciplinary action or remediation imposed.

outcomes.label: Complaint not upheld
outcomes.action: Both parties notified with explanation.

outcomes.label: Complaint withdrawn
outcomes.action: Recorded; underlying issues noted for monitoring.

policies.title: Institutional Accreditation and QAA Compliance Policy
policies.description: Establishes the mandate, scope, self-study report (SSR) process, and compliance requirements for achieving and maintaining institutional accreditation under the UGC Nepal Quality Assurance and Accreditation framework.
policies.scope: The institution as a whole, across all eight UGC QAA criteria.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Coordinates SSR preparation; liaises with UGC accreditation team.
Provide departmental data and evidence for the SSR.
Approves the final SSR submission.
Conducts site visit and validates SSR claims.

policies.decisionContext: Initiated when the institution is eligible for first accreditation or re-accreditation (typically every 5 years). Also triggered by UGC directives or significant institutional change.
constraints: SSR must comprehensively address all eight UGC QAA criteria.
Institution must score a minimum of 60% on each criterion and an overall satisfactory total to achieve accreditation.
Non-accredited institutions cannot add new programs under current UGC policy.

outcomes.label: Accredited
outcomes.action: UGC certificate issued; institution eligible for program expansion and additional grants.

outcomes.label: Conditionally accredited
outcomes.action: Action plan with timeline required.

outcomes.label: Not accredited
outcomes.action: Institution must address deficiencies; re-application allowed after 2 years.

policies.title: Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) Operations Policy
policies.description: Establishes the mandate, composition, meeting schedule, responsibilities, and reporting obligations of the institution's Internal Quality Assurance Cell, which serves as the primary internal mechanism for continuous quality monitoring.
policies.scope: All academic and administrative functions of the institution.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Chairs meetings; prepares Annual Quality Assurance Report (AQAR).
Participate in audits and quality initiatives.
Provides secretarial support; maintains IQAC records.
Reviews AQAR and approves quality improvement plans.

policies.decisionContext: IQAC meets at least quarterly. Special meetings convened following accreditation feedback or significant quality concerns.
legalBasis: UGC Nepal QAA Guidelines — IQAC provisions
constraints: IQAC composition must include at least one student representative and one external member from industry or academia.
AQAR must be submitted to UGC Nepal annually.
IQAC findings are binding on departments with regard to remediation timelines.

outcomes.label: Quality standard met
outcomes.action: Positive finding recorded in AQAR.

outcomes.label: Quality gap identified
outcomes.action: Improvement plan with responsible party and timeline issued.

outcomes.label: Persistent gap
outcomes.action: Escalated to College Principal for institutional-level intervention.

policies.title: Student Learning Outcomes Assessment and Programme Review Policy
policies.description: Mandates the regular assessment of student learning outcomes (SLOs) at course and program level, and defines the programme review cycle, evidence requirements, and use of assessment results for curriculum improvement.
policies.scope: All academic programs across all departments.

keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Define and map SLOs; report assessment results annually.
Design assessments aligned with SLOs; contribute data to program review.
Facilitates 5-year program review; validates SLO assessment methodology.
Use assessment results to drive curriculum decisions.

policies.decisionContext: Annual SLO reporting required. Full program review triggered every 5 years or following significant accreditation findings.
legalBasis: Nepal Education Act provisions on academic quality
constraints: All programs must have documented, measurable SLOs at course and program level.
At least 70% of assessed SLOs must be achieved at the acceptable performance level.
Programs failing to meet this threshold must implement and report on improvement plans.

outcomes.label: SLOs met
outcomes.action: Annual report filed; no additional action.

outcomes.label: SLOs partially met
outcomes.action: Targeted improvement plan developed; reviewed at next cycle.

outcomes.label: SLOs not met
outcomes.action: Program placed on enhanced monitoring; QA Office oversight increased; external review may be commissioned.

policies.title: Complaint Handling and Academic Appeals Policy
policies.description: Provides students and staff with a clear, fair, and accessible mechanism for raising academic and administrative complaints, and for appealing decisions related to grades, admissions, disciplinary actions, and academic standing.
policies.scope: All students and staff of the institution.

keyResponsibilities.role: Complaints Officer (QA Office or nominated administrator)
keyResponsibilities.responsibility: Receives and registers complaints.
Handles first-level academic appeals.
Handles second-level appeals and formal complaints.
Final internal authority for unresolved matters.

policies.decisionContext: Activated when a student or staff member submits a formal complaint or appeal in writing within the specified timeframe.
legalBasis: UGC Nepal QAA Criterion 6 — Student Support
constraints: Complaints must be submitted within 14 days of the triggering event.
Acknowledgment within 3 working days.
First-level response: within 21 days.
Second-level appeal: within 30 days of first-level decision.
All decisions must be provided in writing.

outcomes.label: Complaint upheld
outcomes.action: Remedy applied (grade amendment, policy revision, apology, compensation).

outcomes.label: Complaint partially upheld
outcomes.action: Partial remedy with explanation.

outcomes.label: Complaint not upheld
outcomes.action: Detailed written explanation provided; complainant informed of external escalation options if applicable.
